1/2 🧵
127 years ago today — February 22, 1899 — U.S. forces under Maj. Gen. Elwell S. Otis repelled a major Filipino counterattack in the Second Battle of Manila during the Philippine-American War. 

Amid ongoing clashes after the Spanish cession, (Spanish-American War), 19,000 well-equipped American troops defended the city against ~30,000 poorly-armed insurgents from warring factions, securing key positions with artillery and disciplined fire.

This engagement solidified U.S. control over the archipelago, viewed at the time as vital to counter Japan's Pacific expansions and protect trade routes. A determined step in America's emergence as a global power.

data.raw_text:
(selected excerpts from the diary of Lt. Guy Linley, United States Army)
August 7, 1899. Cotabato Valley, Philippines:
They came over the eastern wall last night in a rush, led by a wild-eyed devil in ragged yellow robes wielding a great curved knife. The bastard was ferocious as a mad dog, some of the boys gave way and ran from him. I came within pistol range as he was dismembering Private Harbin and fired 2 rounds into his upper back. As he turned from his grisly work to face me I fired 2 more, one of which tore apart his lower jaw and another into the neck which ruptured the large artery. He stared at me for a moment, his face horribly disfigured and the lifeblood gushing from the neck wound, then he fled back to the jungle, scrambling over the wall in a blur of yellow robes and splattering blood. That broke the attack but their crazed chanting continued throughout the night.
August 11:
Another attack last night, they did not make it to the walls this time but I spotted the yellow robed man again near the tree line. He had wrapped his lower face in a scarf but by his bearing I knew it was the same man. He did not take his eyes from me during the entire episode. I ordered Cpl. Williams to snipe him and I clearly saw the man stagger from the impact of the bullet, however he stayed on his feet. Williams prepared to fire a second round but Yellow Robe faded into the jungle before he could get a bead on him.
Something is not right here. How Yellow Robe survived the 4 rounds I put into him is beyond imagining. The .38 Long Colt is a much-maligned cartridge but it will surely kill, and this man should be dead considering the amount of his blood still staining the eastern wall.
August 17:
Severed head of Williams found near main gate this morning, eye sockets and mouth stuffed with yellow rags. How Williams was killed outside the walls of the fort is impossible to guess. The only logical answer is that he left the camp willingly,  there is no way he could have been taken by force unless we have traitors among the scouts.
August 18:
Talked to some of the boys who were close to Williams. They told me he had been sleepwalking and was found standing at the wall the last 2 nights before his murder. He proved very hard to wake and mumbled that the yellow-robed man was whispering to him from the jungle. 
August 19:
Some bastard left a yellow rag in my coffee cup this morning. When I find the fellow behind this prank, a day locked in the tool shed should convince him this is no joking matter.
August 21:
Dreamed of Yellow Robe whispering to me last night. Couldn't understand the words but I know he wanted me to come into the jungle.
August 22:
Sleepwalking last night. Dreamed Yellow Robe was calling to me and I attempted to climb the wall. Fought with Morris and 2 others when they tried to restrain me; apparently Morris was forced to give me a crack on the skull with a rifle butt that rendered me completely unconscious.
August 23:
More dreams last night, but this time I saw where Yellow Robe wants me to go, it was a clearing somewhere deep in the jungle. Yellow Robe's followers were wildly dancing around a bonfire while that devil hacked apart some hapless villager and screamed a barbarous incantation at the stars. Williams was among the revelers, his headless body writhing in unholy ecstasy.
Tonight I will handcuff myself to my cot and give the key to Morris. Yellow Robe may call but I will not enter that jungle.
(Note: Guy Linley disappeared the night of August 23, 1899. A trail of blood led from his quarters to the eastern wall of the encampment. He had apparently bitten off his thumb to free himself from handcuffs. Missing and presumed killed in action, Linley's thumb was shipped to his home in Bowling Green, Kentucky and given a proper burial.)

#threatreport:
Earth Kurma is a sophisticated advanced persistent threat (APT) group that has been active since November 2020, primarily targeting Southeast Asia. The group exhibits a strong focus on data exfiltration, utilizing advanced techniques for evasion and persistence. Their operations have shown weak ties to other known APT groups like ToddyCat and Lancefly, further indicating their unique methodology.

This APT employs various tools for lateral movement, including NBTSCAN for NetBIOS scanning, LADON for intranet penetration, and WMIHACKER for lateral movement facilitation. In terms of persistence mechanisms, Earth Kurma utilizes multiple rootkits, backdoors, and loaders. Among their key tools is KRNRAT, a comprehensive backdoor leveraging several open-source projects. Its user-mode agent is injected into "svchost.exe" and operates in a memory-resident manner. Similarly, they use MORIYA, a traffic interceptor that hides malicious payloads within TCP traffic, specifically targeting packets based on their initial bytes for injection.

Earth Kurma's arsenal includes multi-stage, reflective-loading rootkits capable of backdoor operations and memory-resident agents that utilize legitimate services like Cisco Webex and DFSR for command and control communication as well as malware deployment. They have developed a variety of custom loaders and backdoors, such as DOWNBEGIN, which operates through rundll32.exe, offering numerous command capabilities for file management and C&C communication. This variant is particularly notable for its function of creating multiple Cisco Webex meeting rooms to facilitate communication with compromised systems.

The group also utilizes SIMPOBOXSPY, a straightforward tool for uploading files to services like Dropbox, highlighting their reliance on legitimate platforms to exfiltrate data. The variety in their tools—including the reflective-loading capabilities and the specific commands used for file operations—reveals a well-thought-out attack strategy that focuses on both stealth and effectiveness. Earth Kurma's sophisticated methodologies exemplify the ongoing evolution of cyber threats, stressing the need for continuous vigilance and adaptation in security measures.
